source: Neon project shrs-production (orange-dawn-28507285), read directly from the live database
why: The published registers are not the only thing that spends a certificate number.
The Registrar's Office issues certificates through the live system, and on
16 August 2026 it issued three: 000048 (IBT), 000049 (IDD) and 000050 (THN),
each linked to a student record and none revoked. Those numbers are engraved
facts now.
The graduation batch had been planned from the published registers alone, which
end at 000047, so it allocated 000048-000080 and would have claimed all three.
The import would not have corrupted anything - every insert carries ON CONFLICT
DO NOTHING and the end-of-file assertion compares hash, name and Student ID, so
it would have aborted the transaction - but it would have failed at the last
possible moment, in production, for a reason nobody had written down.
So the floor is recorded here as institutional data, with the date and the
source, and the plan takes the greater of this and the registers. A number the
live system has spent can never be re-allocated by a plan computed offline.
readBefore: Re-read this from production before any future batch. It is a snapshot, not a
constant: it was true on the date above and the live system moves without
liveIssuedWhy: Recorded by SERIAL, with no name and no hash. Two reasons.
The ICID assignment must cover every certificate on file, and its assertion
is that no row carries a database-generated default. These three are on file
and are not in any published register here, so without them the assertion
fails against production - correctly, because it would be true that three
certificates carried an accidental permanent identifier.
And the serial is all that is needed: the ICID is UUIDv5 over the stored
serial, so recording the serial reproduces the identifier without this
repository holding anything about the child. Their names, hashes and records
belong to the live system that issued them; nothing here restates them.

reservation.method: setval on stage_certificate_serial_seq, stage_certificates_id_seq and student_identity_seq, executed against production before minting
why: READING A FLOOR IS A RACE. THIS IS THE FIX.
The floor was read at 50, the batch renumbered to 000051-000083, and by the
time the schema migration finished the live system had issued two more and
the sequence stood at 52. The Registrar issues while this pipeline works;
any number chosen from a number read earlier may already be gone.
A certificate number cannot be allocated at import time, because the five
characters engraved on the face are the head of a hash taken over the number
itself - it must be known at mint. So the block is RESERVED in the live
sequence first, then minted into. The live system allocates above the
reservation from that moment, and the race is closed rather than re-run.
Reserve before minting. Do not read a floor and hope.
